scope: Read-only upstream research and local CPU validation. No Azure mutations, GPU allocation, quota requests, deployment or released checkpoint download.

verdicts.unmodified_skt_vllm_on_a100: UNSUPPORTED at the pinned revision; more GPUs do not remove unsupported operators.
verdicts.transformers_bf16_eager_sdpa: Documented alternative with successful miniature CPU execution; full-weight A100 execution, distributed serving and performance UNVERIFIED.
verdicts.custom_sm80_sparse_backend_and_indexer_w: Engineering candidate only, not an existing validated AXK2 deployment.

blockers: FlashMLASparseBackend supports major 9 or 10; FlashInferMLASparseBackend supports major 10; A100 is SM80.
Vendored FlashMLA and DeepGEMM build targets are SM90a and SM100a/f, not SM80. Removing Python capability checks is insufficient.
CUDA SparseAttnIndexer calls DeepGEMM fp8_fp4_mqa_logits and fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits. Disabling DeepGEMM GEMM selection does not substitute an SM80 indexer.
TRITON_MLA inherits non-sparse behavior; AttentionBackend.validate_configuration rejects use_sparse=True.
Transformers BF16 fallback needs approximately 1.4 TB for full weights, plus runtime memory. Its eager/SDPA sparse selection uses dense additive masks, not efficient vLLM sparse kernels.
correction: A100 lacking native FP8 does NOT imply all runtimes must expand weights to BF16. vLLM Marlin has weight-only FP8 W8A16 linear/MoE building blocks including block-128 weights. This does not solve the AXK2 sparse operators or prove end-to-end compatibility.

evidence_tiers.source: Pinned source snapshots, SHA256 hashes, line evidence and extracted Python predicates with mocked device metadata.
evidence_tiers.cpu: 39,328 random parameters, 2 AXK2 layers (dense and grouped MoE), 12 tokens, sparse top-k=4. Eager/SDPA, cached decoding and BF16 finite-output smoke. See axk2-validation-results.json.
evidence_tiers.qwen_azure_sample: Orchestration example only; not AXK2 compatibility evidence.

minimum_future_gpu_plan_not_executed: Use an already available A100 if possible. Install CUDA-enabled PyTorch and pinned Transformers; record driver, CUDA, package versions and measured capability (8, 0).

Run random reduced AXK2 on CUDA in BF16 eager and SDPA, including an original-dimension attention layer (64 heads, qk_nope128, rope64, kv_lora512, v128, index_heads64, index_head_dim128). Use context above index_topk2048, e.g. 4096, to exercise real pruning.

Compare top-k selection and logits with a matching reference, test prefill and cached decode, and record peak allocated/reserved memory, latency and numerical differences. CPU tests alone do not establish GPU tolerance thresholds.
Separately test block-128 FP8 Marlin linear/MoE operators against BF16 references if pursuing a custom vLLM port. Do not expect this to make the existing sparse backend run.

Only after single-GPU operator success, separately approve a reduced-model 2-GPU/2-node communication and sharding test. Full 688B weights and production serving require another capacity/performance decision.

conditional_price_estimate.caveats: Estimate only; excludes disks, network, tax and setup overruns. No VM allocated. Previous subscription inspection found zero A100 family quota; price does not prove quota or capacity.
